stories.title: Supreme Court Seeks Response On Plea To Declare Parts Of MP District Epidemic Prone After Deaths Of 35 Tribal Children

article_sentences: The PIL also seeks provision of drinkable water and the nutritious food for the affected region as well as compensation for the families of deceased children.

A public interest litigation has been filed before the Supreme Court seeking directions to declare the Baiga-dominated Birsa and Baihar blocks of Madhya Pradesh's Balaghat district an epidemic-prone area under the Epidemic Diseases Act, 1897, following deaths of over 30 tribal children due to measles-rubella and severe malnutrition.

A bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V. Mohana today issued notice to the Union, the State, NHRC and other official respondents on the plea after hearing Advocate Varun Thakur for the petitioner.

The petition alleges that administrative negligence, inadequate healthcare facilities, malnutrition and a failure to ensure timely immunisation contributed to the deaths of children in remote tribal settlements.
It seeks compensation for affected families, the provision of safe drinking water and nutritious food, and implementation of government welfare schemes for the tribal community.

“Despite robust statutory frameworks specifically designed to protect their habitat and existence, the State apparatus has manifested a colossal systemic failure, allowing a treatable viral infection to decimate an already fragile population.

Despite explicit, written warnings submitted to the district administration and public representatives as early as January 2026, the State apparatus remained in a bureaucratic slumber”, the plea states.
More than 35 children belonging to the Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Group (PVTG) have reportedly died in the affected areas following an outbreak of measles-rubella and severe malnutrition.
The petition alleges that the administration failed to undertake adequate disease surveillance, provide essential medicines and deploy medical teams despite being alerted to the situation.

The petition also challenges an order issued by the Additional District Magistrate of Balaghat on September 3 under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 prohibiting citizens, journalists and healthcare workers from photographing, recording videos or reels, or publishing information about conditions inside public offices and health facilities on social media.
The petition contends that the restriction is meant to suppress evidence of administrative failures and infringes the constitutional right to freedom of speech and expression.
Notably, the Balaghat administration withdrew the September 3 order within hours of issuing it, stating that it had been issued in haste and was not intended to prevent media coverage.

stories.headline: Saudi authorities say 3 killed in Houthi-claimed attacks on Riyadh airport
stories.title: Saudi authorities say 3 killed in Houthi-claimed attacks on Riyadh airport
stories.summary: Beirut, Oct 9: An airline pilot was among three Saudi citizens killed in attacks targeting Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport and a Saudia aircraft, the kingdom's civil aviation authority said on Friday. Several people “of different nationalities” were wounded. The attacks on Thursday were the deadliest in Saudi Arabia since the kingdom and allied forces in neighbouring Yemen launched a major military offensive against Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels last weekend. They also marked a significant escalation on the latest front in the Iran war, which has kept oil prices and financial markets volatile. Hundreds of flights to and from Riyadh were cancelled on Thursday, according to flight-tracking site FlightAware. The Indian Embassy later said Air India had suspended operations through to Saturday, while the Lufthansa Group said its airlines would suspend flights to Riyadh through to Oct. 16. Pakistan International Airlines has also suspended flights to Riyadh because of the evolving situation in the Middle East, an airline spokesman said. The US Embassy warned citizens on Wednesday of potential airspace closures. Yemen's Houthis claim the attack ---------------------------------------- The first attack on Thursday targeted airport facilities, while the second struck the aircraft, the Saudi statement said. It did not identify those responsible, though the Houthis claimed to have targeted the airport with a ballistic missile. Among the dead was Capt. Hamoud Ali Alkalthami, the Saudia Group said in a statement. It appeared to be the first confirmed attack on the Saudi national carrier since the new offensive began. A separate Saudia Group statement said one of its aircraft was damaged while it was on the ground, with no passengers on board. The aviation statement also said the injuries to citizens and people of other nationalities “ranged from minor to serious.” The Saudia Group statement later said operational activities at the airport had returned to normal. Meanwhile, the Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis said it had destroyed three rocket launch platforms used by the rebels to threaten regional security. Riyadh airport has been repeatedly targeted The airport in the Saudi capital has come under repeated attack in recent days. This week, the Houthis warned global airlines “for the last time” about the potential consequences of operating in Saudi airspace, which they described as a theatre for their military operations. On Wednesday, Saudi officials said Houthi-claimed attacks on airports in Riyadh and Abha had killed three people. Saudi Arabia faces mounting attacks from the Houthis, who declared a blockade of the kingdom earlier this year in response to one imposed on them. The kingdom has sought support from allies, including the United States. Officials said US assistance has included intelligence sharing, target identification and planning for the latest offensive. But President Donald Trump has shown reluctance to expand US military involvement in the Middle East and, for now, has not ordered American forces to resume strikes against the rebels. The offensive aims to retake territory the Houthis seized a month ago along Yemen's western Red Sea coast and the strategic Bab el-Mandeb Strait. Their presence there threatens a crucial alternative shipping route to the Strait of Hormuz, where Iranian attacks on ships have curtailed traffic. (AP)

stories.headline: Indian-origin South African jurist Navi Pillay wins 2026 Nobel Peace Prize
stories.title: Indian-origin South African jurist Navi Pillay wins 2026 Nobel Peace Prize
stories.summary: Norway, Oct 9 : Indian-origin South African jurist and human rights pioneer Navanethem “Navi” Pillay, former United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights, was awarded the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize on Friday for her efforts to promote peace and international law, the Norwegian Nobel Committee announced. In its official announcement on Friday, the committee said Pillay had demonstrated exceptional courage and integrity in advancing a more comprehensive global legal order and had played a significant role in ensuring that war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide are prosecuted. “The Nobel Peace Prize for 2026 goes to a person who with exceptional courage and integrity has led the way towards a more comprehensive global legal order. This year’s laureate has been instrumental in ensuring that war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide are prosecuted,” the press release stated. In a post on X announcing the award, the Nobel Prize account said, “Today Navi Pillay has been awarded the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize for her efforts to promote peace and international law.” The Nobel Committee highlighted Pillay’s long career in advancing universal legal principles, from her early work defending Nelson Mandela and others who opposed apartheid in South Africa to her service as a judge in major international legal cases. “Born into a family of Indian Tamil origin under apartheid in Durban, South Africa, Pillay became a lawyer and legal pioneer, confronting deep structural discrimination, segregation and exclusion,” the committee said. Pillay has served as a judge on South Africa’s High Court, the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda and the International Criminal Court. She also served as the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights and, until recently, chaired the UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory. She is currently a judge at the International Court of Justice in the case in which Myanmar stands accused of genocide, according to the Nobel Committee. The committee noted that Pillay had helped demonstrate how legal measures could prevent acts of war and violence while strengthening international legal institutions. In a post on X, the Nobel Prize account emphasised the importance of international law in addressing conflicts peacefully. “More and more conflicts are being addressed through diplomacy, treaties and legal mechanisms, rather than threats, violence and warfare. International law is a foundation for a more peaceful world,” the post said. It added, “At a time of existential challenges - including more wars and conflicts than the world has seen in a long time – international law is no longer just a supplement to peace and security. It is an absolute necessity.” The Nobel Committee also highlighted Pillay’s contribution to landmark legal developments in the prosecution of sexual violence and genocide. “When the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda established that rape and sexual violence could constitute a crime against humanity – as well as genocide - her influence was a significant factor,” the committee said. It added that Pillay was instrumental in a separate legal breakthrough in the same case, in which a defendant faced charges of incitement to commit genocide purely based on "spreading propaganda". The committee said Pillay had held states and national leaders accountable while bringing hope to victims of violence and conflict. Throughout her career, she has emphasised the responsibility of individuals and states to comply with the rule of law. The award also comes amid what the committee described as growing pressure on the international legal system and its institutions. “We see a shift towards power politics at the expense of legal frameworks and global respect for law and justice. Whenever might overtakes right, it undermines stability, trust and peaceful co-existence,” the press release stated. Explaining the significance of the award, the committee said, “In awarding this year’s Nobel Peace Prize, the Norwegian Nobel Committee wants to remind the world that the rule of law - national and international - underpins the system we have set up to ensure peace and resolve conflicts non-violently. Peace requires justice.” The committee further said that Pillay’s career demonstrated the importance of protecting and expanding international legal principles. “Navi Pillay’s commitment to justice and human dignity is a source of hope and inspiration to all who seek to bring about a more peaceful world,” it said. The Nobel Committee said the 2026 Peace Prize was rooted in Alfred Nobel’s will, highlighting Pillay’s contribution to strengthening fraternity between nations and advancing the use of tribunals to promote peace and justice.

stories.title: Supreme Court declines plea on Tamil Nadu Speaker's reprieve for 21 AIADMK MLAs
stories.summary: Supreme Court declines plea on Tamil Nadu Speaker's reprieve for 21 AIADMK MLAs
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
event term: 'supreme court' in summary weight 26.4
article_sentences: The Supreme Court refused to hear a plea against the Tamil Nadu Speaker dropping disqualification proceedings against 21 AIADMK MLAs.
The bench said only the party or an authorised legislator could press the grievance, while leaving larger legal questions open.

The Supreme Court on Friday refused to entertain a plea against Tamil Nadu Assembly Speaker's decision to drop disqualification proceedings against 21 AIADMK MLAs who had voted in favour of the TVK government during a confidence motion despite the party whip.
A bench led by Chief Justice Surya Kant said it would not interfere with the Madras High Court order dismissing the public interest litigation filed by P V Selvakumar.
At the same time, the bench said it was leaving the questions of law open and could examine them in an appropriate case.

During the hearing, the court repeatedly questioned whether Selvakumar had the standing to pursue the matter, saying he was neither a legislator nor an authorised representative who could press for disqualification proceedings.
Appearing for Selvakumar, advocate.
Nina Nariman said he was an AIADMK member and a voter concerned about the conduct of the legislators.
Justice Joymalya Bagchi observed that proceedings under the 10th Schedule of the Constitution had to be pursued by a member of the House.
"We are fully with you that the sanctity of constitutional mandate must be preserved.
But we must understand the working of a democratic system," the judge said.
The bench also noted that the AIADMK leadership appeared to have condoned the conduct of the MLAs and said the grievance should be raised by the party or its authorised representatives.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Restrains Delhi Private Hospital From Discharging Acid Attack Survivor, Directs Treatment Regardless Of Cost
stories.title: Supreme Court Restrains Delhi Private Hospital From Discharging Acid Attack Survivor, Directs Treatment Regardless Of Cost
stories.summary: The Court allowed the hospital to forward the bills to the Supreme Court for reimbursement directions.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
event term: 'supreme court' in summary weight 26.4
article_sentences: The Court allowed the hospital to forward the bills to the Supreme Court for reimbursement directions.

The Supreme Court today directed Sir Ganga Ram Hospital in Delhi to provide all necessary treatment, regardless of cost, to an acid attack survivor admitted there after sustaining damage to both her eyes.
A bench of CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana passed the order when the matter was mentioned around 4 PM by a woman appearing in-person on behalf of the survivor.
The woman informed the Court that the acid attack survivor was currently in Ganga Ram Hospital but was being threatened with discharge.
She alleged that the hospital was claiming that it was not "specialized" in the required treatment.
The woman further claimed that Apollo Hospital was also consulted, but it declined to take in the survivor.
It was further submitted that the survivor did not wish to go to a government hospital.
The woman highlighted that vide its orders, the Supreme Court has given acid attack survivors the right to avail treatment in any private hospital of their choice.
"Ganga Ram mei hai, toh wahin rakhte hain (if she is in Ganga Ram, then let her be there only)", the CJI responded.
The woman in-person agreed, while submitting that if at all the survivor is to be transferred out of Ganga Ram hospital, she should be allowed treatment in Apollo Hospital.

Ultimately, the Court directed the management of Sir Ganga Ram hospital to take in the survivor as an indoor patient and provide all facilities, including medicines and plastic surgery, as and when required, irrespective of the cost to be incurred on the treatment.

As against allegation of the hospital forcing the survivor to leave the hospital, the Court added that the hospital shall not discharge her until doctors certify that she is fit for discharge and will require only outdoor treatment.

article_sentences: India’s logistics sector is expected to double in size to $600 billion by 2031-32 from around $300 billion currently, driven by infrastructure development, policy reforms and improved connectivity, said Subhash Chandra Karol, Director, Logistics Division, Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT).
Logistics contributed more than 13 per cent to India’s GDP and played a critical role in supporting manufacturing growth.

The two sectors were complementary, making efficient logistics infrastructure essential to strengthening the country’s manufacturing ecosystem, he said while addressing at PRISM 2026 – Powering Recognition: India’s Skill Movement, hosted by the Logistics Sector Skill Council (LSC) in association with National Skill Development Council on Friday.
A study conducted by DPIIT in 2025 estimated India’s logistics costs at around 8 per cent of GDP, challenging the earlier perception that they accounted for 13-14 per cent.
The reduction reflects the impact of government reforms and efforts to improve logistics efficiency, although the official noted that comparable estimates had not been available earlier.
India has also improved its position in the Logistics Performance Index (LPI), moving from 46th in 2018 to 30th.
The government aims to bring the country into the top 25 within the next five years, said Karol.
Infrastructure connectivity remains central to improving logistics efficiency, with better links needed between manufacturing hubs, consumption centres and last-mile destinations.
The government launched PM Gati Shakti in 2021 as a digital platform to coordinate infrastructure planning across ministries.

The platform helps identify gaps in connectivity, locate underserved areas and anticipate implementation hurdles, including forest areas and restricted zones, before projects reach the execution stage.
This enables authorities to plan clearances in advance and reduce delays during implementation, the official said.
The pace of road construction has increased from around 5-6 km a day to more than 15 km a day on average, according to the official.

stories.title: Supreme Court raps Kerala over Raman elephant custody, seeks medical report
stories.summary: Supreme Court raps Kerala over Raman elephant custody, seeks medical report
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
event term: 'supreme court' in summary weight 26.4
article_sentences: The Supreme Court questioned Kerala's failure to take custody of Raman and sought his latest medical report.
The hearing sharpened concerns over compliance, welfare monitoring and alleged commercial exploitation.

The Supreme Court on Friday pulled up the Kerala government for not complying with its order to take over the custody of Raman, described as the tallest elephant in the state, and asked for the animal's latest medical report.
The court was told that Raman remained with his caretaker because he was in musth, a condition unique to elephants in which testosterone levels rise sharply, and could not be shifted.
A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu said the state had not acted in line with its earlier directions on the elephant's upkeep.
It also questioned whether the authorities were monitoring Raman's health and directed the Kerala government to place a recent medical report on record.
During the hearing, the caretaker's side told the court that Raman had been treated with love and care.
Justice Datta responded sharply, saying, "Love, care and for the purpose of earning money by defying the Supreme Court's restraint orders.
We quite understand what love and affection are.
We are not going to hear you." The bench also asked the state's counsel, "Are you monitoring the condition of the elephant or not?
The last medical report means you have not checked him after 24th June?"
The court then directed the state government to submit Raman's latest medical report.

stories.title: Telangana CM Revanth to review El Nino impact, drought conditions on October 12
stories.summary: The action plan prepared by Telangana Cabinet sub-committee on drought mitigation, along with relief measures likely to be examined
reasons: source: event has 2 copies, primary source counted once
corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy will hold a special meeting with Ministers on October 12 to review the impact of El Nino and the prevailing rainfall deficit in Telangana, with a focus on relief measures for farmers and steps to address emerging water and power requirements.

The meeting is expected to take stock of conditions in areas that have received insufficient rainfall, the difficulties faced by farmers and the immediate interventions required to mitigate the impact of the dry spell.
Agriculture, irrigation, drinking water supply and the rising demand for electricity will be among the key issues on the agenda.
The move comes after an extensive discussion on the rainfall deficit at the recent State Cabinet meeting.
Telangana has recorded 17% less rainfall than normal, with drought-like conditions prevailing in nearly 235 mandals, according to official estimates cited by the government.
The State government has already adopted a resolution in the Legislative Assembly urging the Centre to declare drought-affected mandals and extend adequate financial assistance.
It has also sought a special package of Rs.
20,000 crore to help the State tackle the impact of the deficient rainfall.

The meeting on Tuesday is likely to examine the action plan prepared by the Cabinet sub-committee on drought mitigation, along with relief measures that need to be taken up in rainfall-deficient areas.
Suggestions emerging from political parties, consultations with farmers’ organisations and inputs from experts in various sectors are also expected to figure in the discussions.

stories.headline: Aravalli conservation: SC panel to survey forests and mines in Rajasthan
stories.title: Aravalli conservation: SC panel to survey forests and mines in Rajasthan
stories.summary: Jaipur, Oct 9 : The Supreme Court-appointed High-Powered Committee (HPC), tasked with examining the definition, ecological status and conservation of the Aravalli mountain range, will visit Rajasthan’s Vagad region from October 11 to 13. The committee will inspect the Paldeval-Sarkan area of Dungarpur district and the Kevadiya-Kothara area of Banswara district to assess ground realities concerning mining, forests, land use and the livelihoods of local communities, particularly tribal populations. The visit follows the committee’s tour of the Aravalli region in Gujarat from October 8 to 10. During its Rajasthan visit, the panel will conduct field inspections and interact with local residents and other stakeholders. Its findings will contribute to a comprehensive report that the Supreme Court has directed it to submit by November 30 this year. In an order dated May 25, 2026, the Supreme Court constituted a five-member High-Powered Committee chaired by the Director General of the Indian Council of Forestry Research and Education (ICFRE). The committee was tasked with independently examining the previously-formulated definition of the Aravalli range and the process used to demarcate the hills based on that definition. The exercise is intended to assess the region’s ecological characteristics and address concerns relating to its conservation. The committee’s latest visit will focus on areas where the relationship between the Aravalli landscape, forest ecosystems, wildlife, mining activities and local livelihoods is particularly significant. The Rajasthan government has mobilised the Forest Department and local field officials ahead of the committee’s visit. A senior Forest Department official will serve as the field coordinator, while Deputy Conservators of Forests (DCFs) and other field personnel from Dungarpur and Banswara will accompany the panel during its inspections. The arrangements are intended to facilitate site visits, provide relevant field information and enable direct interaction between the committee and local stakeholders. The committee had earlier undertaken a five-day tour of Rajasthan, during which it conducted field inspections and consulted stakeholders at several locations. However, concerns were raised that participation had been inadequate, particularly among rural residents and tribal communities. This prompted calls for another ground-level assessment in southern Rajasthan, with greater emphasis on hearing directly from the people most affected by decisions concerning the Aravalli region. In its order dated September 7, the Supreme Court clarified that the committee must provide sufficient opportunities for all relevant stakeholders, including tribal communities in Rajasthan and Gujarat, to express their views. The panel is expected to incorporate these perspectives into its final assessment, which must be submitted to the Court by November 30. During the upcoming inspections, the committee will examine several aspects of the region’s environmental and economic landscape, including mining and quarrying activities, including stone-crushing operations, forest cover, water sources and surrounding ecological conditions, existing land-use patterns and their environmental implications, the impact of mining and land-use practices on local residents and tribal livelihoods. The committee will also seek feedback from environmentalists, subject experts, mining leaseholders, villagers, farmers, labourers and tribal communities. Evening consultations are planned in both districts, with approximately three hours allocated for discussions with local residents and other stakeholders on each day. According to the proposed schedule, the committee will complete its Gujarat tour by October 10 before entering southern Rajasthan on October 11. On October 11, there will be field inspections in the Paldeval-Sarkan area of Dungarpur district, followed by consultations with stakeholders. On October 12, inspection of the Kevadiya-Kothara area in Banswara district will be made followed by discussions with local communities and other stakeholders. October 13 will mark the final day of the scheduled Rajasthan visit. The inspections are expected to provide the committee with a clearer understanding of local environmental conditions, mining-related concerns and the socio-economic realities of communities living in the region. The findings will form part of the broader assessment of the Aravalli hills’ definition, demarcation and conservation. The committee’s report, due by November 30 this year, will be submitted to the Supreme Court for further consideration. --IANS

stories.headline: Supreme Court Issues Notice On Plea To Fill Vacancies In Electricity Regulatory Commissions In 15 States, J&K
stories.title: Supreme Court Issues Notice On Plea To Fill Vacancies In Electricity Regulatory Commissions In 15 States, J&K
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Friday (October 9) issued notice on a PIL filed by NGO Energy Watchdog over prolonged vacancies and absence of legally qualified members in State Electricity Regulatory Commissions of 15 States and Jammu and Kashmir.
A bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V. Mohana issued notice.
The plea contends that the prolonged vacancies amount to violation of Article 21 of the Constitution, the Electricity Act, 2003 and the Supreme Court's 2018 judgment in State of Gujarat.
Utility Users' Welfare Association.
“The continuing failure to provide a lawfully constituted Commission strikes at consumers' access to justice under Articles 14 and 21.

In the absence of the mandated person of law, consumers cannot obtain lawful adjudication of complaints invoking Section 142 of the Electricity Act against distribution licensees where the statutory conditions for such proceedings are fulfilled.
Consumers' access to that remedy cannot be made dependent upon indefinite executive inaction in filling the offices of the very institution entrusted with enforcing the law.
In Tamil Nadu, the complete absence of Members disables both adjudicatory and regulatory functioning”, the plea contends.

The petition seeks directions to the concerned State Governments and authorities to ensure that the Commissions are constituted as per Sections 82, 84 and 85 of the Electricity Act and the 2018 judgment.

In that case, the Court held that a suitably qualified person of law must be a member of a State Electricity Regulatory Commission and every bench exercising adjudicatory functions must include such a member.

The petition has been filed against West Bengal, Madhya Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, Kerala, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, Meghalaya, Sikkim, Manipur, Mizoram and Nagaland, and the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir, which is served by the Joint Electricity Regulatory Commission for Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh.

The petition contends that the vacancies and deficiencies in the composition of these Commissions affect their ability to discharge regulatory and adjudicatory functions and undermine electricity consumers' access to effective legal remedies.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Pulls Up Kerala Govt Over Compliance With Direction On Elephant's Upkeep
stories.title: Supreme Court Pulls Up Kerala Govt Over Compliance With Direction On Elephant's Upkeep
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court today(October 9) pulled up the Kerala government for not showing compliance with its June order to take over the custody of Raman, a captive elephant known to be the tallest in Kerala.

It may be recalled that in June, the Court held a Kerala resident, Krishnankutty, guilty of contempt for violating an undertaking that the elephant would not be subjected to commercial exploitation pending the adjudication of the present dispute.
Subsequently, it directed the State to take over the custody of Raman and house it in an appropriate rescue or rehabilitation centre.
Today, the matter came up before a bench comprising Justice Dipankar Datta and Justice Sheel Nagu.
When Justice Datta asked about the whereabouts of the elephant, the caretaker informed that it was with him because the elephant was in a state of musth and couldn't be shifted.
The State's counsel also supported this argument, but the petitioner's counsel opposed it, stating that whenever there is an order to shift the elephant, the state of musth is "induced artificially."
This compelled Justice Datta to remark: "We will not allow you[the caretaker] to touch it[the elephant]".
The caretaker submitted that the elephant has been treated with love and care.
But Justice Datta responded that the musth issue had happened only for a few months and questioned what steps have been taken subsequent to the Court's order.
He also told the caretaker: "Love, care and for the purpose of earning money by defying the Supreme Court's restraint orders.
We quite understand what love and affection is.
We are not going to hear you."

stories.headline: Supreme Court Stays Trial In Criminal Defamation Cases Filed By BJP Leader Ramesh Bhiduri, Nephew Against TV Today Network
stories.title: Supreme Court Stays Trial In Criminal Defamation Cases Filed By BJP Leader Ramesh Bhiduri, Nephew Against TV Today Network
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court today stayed the trial in criminal defamation cases filed against TV Today Network Ltd., which owns Aaj Tak and the India Today group, filed by BJP leader Ramesh Bidhuri and his nephew Rajpal Poswal.
The case concerns alleged defamatory news connecting Bhiduri's nephew to a gang rape and abduction case.
The case relates to a news broadcast aired in 2011 concerning a gang rape and abduction case involving an individual described as the brother-in-law of Bidhuri's nephew.
At the time, Bidhuri was an elected MLA from the Tughlakabad constituency.
The broadcast criticised alleged police inaction in arresting the individual, while his co-accused had already been taken into custody.
Complaints were filed by Bidhuri and Poswal alleging that the telecast was malicious, defamatory, misleading and intended to tarnish their reputation before the public.
On November 2025, the Delhi High Court dismissed petitions filed by TV Today challenging a trial court order which had rejected its applications for discharge.
The High Court held that the Metropolitan Magistrate did not have the power to discharge an accused in a summons triable case.
The High Court rejected the contention that the Magistrate could invoke inherent jurisdiction under Section 251 of the CrPC to drop proceedings.
The High Court further held that Section 251 of the CrPC does not empower a Magistrate to undertake a mini-trial or evaluate defences on merits at that stage.
The stage for consideration of such issues would arise only when evidence is led, the HC stated.
